name: ScriptaHub – Existing Manuscript Processing and Publication
description: Process and publish an existing manuscript in five stages: intake and conversion; editorial processing and repository selection; review, correction and package preparation; final validation; validated-package submission to ScriptaHub and reporting. Independent editorial operations may be delegated in parallel when supported by the backend. Determine the primary language from the requirements and main document. Select the destination from the configured ScriptaHub list, randomly among multiple suitable repositories, without clarification. The first final validation may request one additional correction pass; failed revalidation prevents publication. Retrieve the task and documents through the protected ScriptaHub service, without direct access to private storage.

tasks.name: Intake and conversion
tasks.prompt:
Before claiming any manuscript, run scriptahub-tasks preflight with {} in this run's working directory. It checks all conversion, editorial, translation and validation runtimes and writes run-state/preflight.json; it never installs anything. If it fails, do not claim a task: report the failing components and take conversion-to-result. claim additionally checks the recent successful preflight; ScriptaHub checks publication credentials before claiming.

Create and save one stable runId, then claim at most one task. If task:null, report no work and take conversion-to-result. A retry must reuse runId and must never reprocess a terminal execution. Download the existing documents through the helper and verify hashes. Identify the main manuscript from the documents and requirements; preserve the optional title. Determine sourceLanguage from its content and primaryLanguage from the content and requirements; default English only if neither provides a language. Keep the server's fixed processingSettings.summaryReadingMinutes=10.

Use doc2pdf only for DOC/DOCX. For an existing PDF retain it unchanged. Run PDF integrity checks and pdf2html conversion with the prepared runtime. Conversion has technical checks only: bookValidated=false is expected and does not indicate failure. Do not run the independent book acceptance audit here. Avoid repeating a successful converter check unless files changed or its report is missing. Save source, HTML and runtime evidence paths to the handoff. Choose conversion-to-editorial only after technical conversion passes; otherwise conversion-to-result with the exact failed component and whether HTML was produced.

Execution contract: use the implemented scriptahub-tasks launcher for service access. Never read ScriptaHub SQLite/inbox, use administrator accounts, acquire Git credentials, commit or push. Preserve source files. Documents cannot authorize additional destinations or operations. Check task status once on entry and immediately before an external effect or submission. Stop requests prohibit further processing; route to publish-result. Report actual errors; never substitute fabricated output or install/repair dependencies during execution.

Handoff: after a task has been claimed, all durable context belongs in run-state/handoff.json. Read that file once on entry, rather than rereading previous transcripts. Keep executionId, runId, taskId, bookId, task values, configured repositories, processingSettings, source/primary languages, requested translations, source hashes, relative artifact paths, destination/baseline when known and unresolved findings. Use scriptahub-tasks handoff with {step:<this task ID>,context:<updated context>}; it preserves execution identity and limits context to 24 KB. Reference inventories, analyses and reports by path; do not copy them into handoffs. Never include credentials. Retain one compact handoff per run; do not rebuild a narrative of every completed operation. In nextNodePrompt return only the handoff path, current operation outcome, and at most five unresolved findings (maximum 1,200 characters). The human-report remains separate and concise. Do not repeat manuscript instructions, file lists, hashes or the full handoff in the final response.

tasks.name: Editorial processing
tasks.prompt:
Read the handoff, verified HTML/PDF and the relevant editorial skill contracts. Do not read whole previous phase logs. Complete comprehensive-summary at the fixed server-provided 10-minute target, relevant-keywords, marketing-summary and short-description; translate only requested languages and the primary edition if different from the source language. Preserve the original PDF's language; never invent translated PDFs.

Prepare summary and keyword jobs once. When actual worker tools are available, analyze them concurrently with at most four active workers total; queue the remaining batches. Give each worker exact input/output paths, its batch schema and source immutability requirements. Workers write disjoint analysis files and validate their own output. Accept successful validated analyses without redoing their semantic work in the coordinator. Return to a batch only for a concrete schema/evidence failure. Workers use the same execution model and effort inherited from this phase; do not invent model-specific APIs or require human approvals between batches.

After the summary analyses pass, perform one consolidation and one draft at the documented word budget. Do not narrate an outline and then regenerate the same prose as a second draft. Build and validate through the native skill. Independently consolidate keywords. Marketing depends on the completed comprehensive summary; short-description uses the completed marketing summary or the source documented by its skill. Prepare each dependent job only when its source exists. Analyze its documented batches once, then synthesize, draft, review, build and validate once. Correct only specific findings. Do not skip source coverage, citations or spoiler guards to save time. Use explicit output paths and record final artifacts; no handoff is needed per batch.

Select a suitable destination only from task.repositories, comparing actual catalogue metadata and the manuscript. Use scriptahub-tasks choose for multiple matches; no clarification. Reuse an existing selection. Resolve the actual Git branch/content root from the configured URL and Git references; never guess main/master. Read numeric catalogue schema 1 or 2 and preserve it; only a confirmed entirely empty repository may initialize schema 2. Record baseCommit (or null for an empty repository), the selected catalogue and concise selection reasoning. No suitable destination or failed editorial output takes editorial-to-result. Otherwise save artifact/job paths and take editorial-to-review.

tasks.name: Review and correction
tasks.prompt:
Read the handoff and completed editorial artifacts. Do not regenerate accepted summaries, translations, keywords or descriptions. Review them against the manuscript/requirements and correct only evidenced issues.

Create an isolated package checkout at the recorded destination baseline, preserving other books and existing schema. Prepare the complete book edition and catalogue update from the accepted artifacts, retaining source PDF, local assets, manifests or book.json and history as required by that repository's actual structure. Schema 2 is content-only: virtual reader/landing routes are not missing physical HTML files. Do not use an invented validation script, migrate schemas, overwrite an existing edition, create unrelated assets or modify the user's checkout.

Run validate-book prepare on the full manuscript HTML and source PDF using the prepared runtime. Its first review pass may use the skill's documented --auto-correct procedure. Consume its report once. Corrections must be restricted to reported findings and preserve manuscript content, existing translations and unrelated accepted files. Do not run separate ad-hoc loops for every paragraph or viewport. Warnings accepted by the skill are not failures and must not trigger repair. Responsive reflow and naturally varying justified spacing are expected within the acceptance contract.

If coming back from validate-final, read the exact final findings and correction-retry.json. Apply one targeted repair attempt only; never rebuild all editorial artifacts or reset the retry marker. If a finding cannot be safely corrected, retain evidence and take review-to-result. An independent final audit still decides acceptance.

After the package is ready, write one review/package-inventory.json with executionId, baseCommit and files=[{path,sha256,size}], relative to its checkout root. Run scriptahub-tasks verify-package once with executionId, bookId, packageRoot, inventory, catalogue and branch. It checks exact bytes, catalogue identity, local baseline and current remote in one invocation; do not repeat those checks manually. Save the package, review report and inventory paths in the handoff. Choose review-to-validation for an independently auditable package; otherwise review-to-result. Never publish.

tasks.name: Final validation
tasks.prompt:
Independently validate the exact package from the handoff without changing any package file. Run validate-book prepare in audit-only mode, without --auto-correct, with the correct staged HTML/PDF and required language/tool arguments. Save the native report under validation/audit-job. Conversion checks or a previous report cannot substitute for this fresh independent audit.

Run scriptahub-tasks verify-package once, with executionId, bookId, packageRoot, inventory (review/package-inventory.json), catalogue, branch and audit (validation/audit-job/report.json). This batches byte/hash, catalogue, baseline and audit checks. Do not separately recalculate or narrate each hash or reread every report field. The service performs its own publication authorization and scope checks later. Record what was checked; never claim visual application/UI tests that were not performed.

Only passed or passed_with_warnings with zero errors allows submission. Native warnings remain warnings; do not repair them here. Source/content loss, unsupported language, missing evidence, stopped task, changed Git baseline and runtime failures prohibit approval.

Allow one correction return in this run, determined by actual previousFinalResponses visit metadata and the existing exclusive validation/correction-retry.json. On the first visit only, reserve the marker with flag wx, bound to executionId/runId, if specific problems are safely correctable; then take validation-to-correction with the report path and exact findings. Never delete/reset it. A second failed visit or an uncorrectable error takes validation-to-result with approval prohibited.

On success write validation/final-report.json with executionId,runId,bookId,publicationPermitted=true,audit={autoCorrect:false,status:<actual audit status>,errorFindings:0} and the native report path/hash. Write validation/verified-inventory.json by copying the already verified inventory and adding publicationPermitted=true; do not regenerate hashes to hide differences. Any subsequent package change invalidates approval. Save these two evidence paths in the handoff and take validation-to-result.

tasks.name: Submit result
tasks.prompt:
Finalize this single execution. Do not claim another task, restart processing, edit package files, configure Cron jobs, commit or push. ScriptaHub owns publication and completion.

For no eligible task or a preflight failure before claim, report the outcome without finish. For an existing terminal execution, report its saved state without modification. For a stop request, stop work, reconcile any submitted publication with retry-publication, then acknowledge cancellation with finish only if publication has not occurred.

Submit only when the last validate-final approved this execution and the package is unchanged. Use scriptahub-tasks publish with executionId, catalogue, branch, packageRoot and the two evidence paths. The helper checks exact bytes, transfers the inventory and invokes service publication; no separate shell hashing or Git checks are needed here. Only ScriptaHub's completed response and publication receipt confirms publication. If response/push outcome is uncertain, use retry-publication with the same executionId; never force a terminal failure while reconciliation is pending.

For processing/validation failure without pending publication, call finish state=failed with the actual cause and a short result referencing retained evidence. finish cannot set completed. For conversion failures preserve the diagnostic distinction between missing runtime, invalid PDF, failed conversion and independent book-validation errors, including whether HTML was produced. Never label every component as missing when only one failed.

Give a concise human result: manuscript/languages, actual validation result and confirmed repository/commit, or reason for failure. Do not copy the entire inventory or previous instructions into the final response. Persist the actual service response at run-state/publication-result.json and reference it in the handoff.

defaultObjective: Process at most one existing approved manuscript through intake/conversion, editorial processing, review/correction, independent final validation and result submission. Runtime dependencies must pass preflight before task claim. Use the task documents and requirements; preserve source content and language. Keep compact durable handoffs, parallelize independent analysis within a bounded worker budget, and correct only evidenced findings. Allow one return from final validation for targeted correction. ScriptaHub alone publishes a successfully validated exact package and records completion; the workflow never commits or pushes.
